questions.q: In Scenario 1, what was the actual root cause of the sudden drop in automatic reconciliation match rate?
options: The bank statement file failed to import
The bank changed its ACH credit transaction code and the mapping table wasn't updated
The GL cash account was deleted
The reconciliation rule set was removed from the bank account
questions.explain: The bank switched its ACH credit code from 475 to 478, and the existing mapping table only recognized 475 — a classic unmapped transaction code problem.

questions.q: What was the correct fix for Scenario 1, rather than manually reconciling each affected statement line?
options: Delete the bank account and recreate it
Switch the bank account to a different statement file format
Add a mapping for the new code once, so the backlog reconciles automatically on the next run
questions.explain: Fixing the root cause (the missing code mapping) once resolves the whole backlog automatically, rather than patching each line by hand.

questions.q: In Scenario 2, what was the actual cause of the cash position looking $28,000 too low?
options: A missing inflow external transaction that was never created on the To account of a transfer
A currency conversion error in Cash Forecasting
questions.explain: The outflow leg reconciled, but the matching inflow external transaction on the To account was never created — a process miss rather than a bank error.

questions.q: Which chapter of this course covered the reconciliation rules and matching rules used to diagnose Scenario 1?
questions.explain: Chapter 3 (Reconciliation) covered rule sets, matching rules, and the mechanics behind automatic reconciliation's match rate.

questions.q: Which course comes next in the Financial Operations stage of the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path?
